title: Musubee core API
description: Contract between the Musubee core and its user interfaces (docs/ADR/0012-core-api-contract.md). Requests, responses and events are JSON documents in UTF-8. $defs/Commands lists every command with its params and result, $defs/Events every event with its data. Every object is exact for this version (additionalProperties: false), but consumers must ignore fields, event types and enum values they do not know: a newer core may send them.

Request.description: Envelope of a request sent to the core.

id.description: Chosen by the caller and copied into the response.

params.description: The params of the command; may be omitted when they are all optional.

Response.description: Envelope of the core's answer to a request: exactly one of result and error. The id is 0 when the request could not be parsed.

Event.description: Envelope of an event sent by the core.

Commands.description: Every command, by name, with the schema of its params and of its result.

core.hello.description: Returns the versions of the API and of the core. A user interface calls it first and refuses a core whose major API version differs from its own.

networks.list.description: Lists the networks this core can connect to.

accounts.list.description: Lists the accounts the user added, on every network.

accounts.verify.description: Verifies this device for a Matrix account with the account's recovery key (the key its Matrix app gave when secure backup was set up), then restores the account's key backup, so that older encrypted messages and other clients trust this device. The key is neither stored nor logged. Fails with invalid_params for a key that is not the account's, and unsupported for an account without secure backup or of another network. Since API 1.15.

accounts.verification.description: Verifies this device for a Matrix account by comparing emoji with another device of the account: start asks the other devices; accept takes another device's request; confirm says the emoji match; cancel ends it (they did not match, or the user gave up). Each step comes as an account.verification event. Fails with unsupported for other networks, and invalid_params for an action that does not fit the current step. Since API 1.22.

accounts.logout.description: Logs an account out of its network and removes it from this device, with the conversations only it reached. The account first appears once more, in an account.updated event with the state logged_out. Since API 1.1.

login.start.description: Starts adding an account with one of the network's login flows, and returns the first step. With an account_id, logs in to that account again instead (for example in state bad_credentials), keeping its conversations: the flow must be one of the account's network. A login that ends on another account adds it and leaves this one as it was. Since API 1.5 for account_id.

login.submit.description: Submits the fields of a user_input step, and returns the next step.

login.wait.description: Waits until a display_and_wait step is done (for example a QR code scanned on the phone), and returns the next step. Unlike other commands it has no time limit: login.cancel ends it.

login.cancel.description: Abandons a login process. Cancelling a finished or unknown process is not an error.

conversations.list.description: Lists the conversations of every account, or of one account, the most recently active first. Without a limit, returns them all; with one, returns a page and a cursor to the next. Ordered by activity since API 1.3. Since API 1.24, the first page (no cursor) starts with every pinned conversation, the most recently active first, and the pages hold the others only: a page can then be shorter than its limit and still have a next one.

conversations.typing.description: Tells the conversation's network that the user types (again while typing, every few seconds, as networks forget it), or stopped. Networks that do not show typing ignore it. Since API 1.20.

conversations.markUnread.description: Marks a conversation as unread (marked_unread), on this device, until it is read again. The conversation is then sent again in a conversation.updated event, if it was not marked already. Since API 1.18.

conversations.mute.description: Mutes a conversation until a time, or until it is unmuted (until_ms -1), or unmutes it (until_ms 0). A muted conversation still counts its unread messages, but the apps do not notify the user of them. The network is told when it supports mutes, so that its other apps stay quiet too. The conversation is then sent again in a conversation.updated event, if its mute changed. Since API 1.23.

conversations.pin.description: Pins a conversation at the top of the inbox, or unpins it. The network is told when it supports it (Matrix's favourite tag), and a pin set in the network's other apps shows here. The conversation is then sent again in a conversation.updated event, if its pin changed. Since API 1.24.

conversations.delete.description: Deletes a conversation for the user, on the network too: its history goes from this device and, as the network allows, from the user's other apps; the other people keep theirs. Only when Conversation.actions.delete_chat says the network allows it. Resolves once the network deleted it (a conversation.deleted event follows); fails if the network refuses or does not answer within 30 seconds. Since API 1.25.

conversations.leave.description: Leaves a group on its network, then removes it from this device with its messages (a conversation.deleted event follows). Only when Conversation.actions.leave says the network allows it. Resolves once the network answered; fails if it refuses or does not answer within 30 seconds. Since API 1.29.

conversations.archive.description: Archives a conversation, or brings it back, on this device only: no network learns it. An archived conversation comes back by itself when someone writes in it, unless it is muted. The conversation is then sent again in a conversation.updated event, if it changed. Since API 1.31.

conversations.setDraft.description: Keeps the text the user left unsent in a conversation's composer, on this device only (an empty text forgets it): the network never sees it. Sent again in Conversation.draft, but no conversation.updated event follows: the interface that wrote it knows it. Since API 1.30.

conversations.members.description: Lists who is in a conversation, as this device knows it: the user first, then the others by name. The network's bridge is not a member. Since API 1.27.

conversations.markRead.description: Records that the user read a conversation up to a message (by default its last one), and clears its marked_unread flag. The network is told when it supports read receipts. Reading never moves back: a message before the current read position changes nothing. The conversation is then sent again in a conversation.updated event, if its read state changed. Since API 1.4.

messages.list.description: Returns the latest messages of a conversation, or the ones before a cursor, oldest first.

messages.search.description: Finds the messages on this device whose text (as edited) or caption contains a text, in one conversation or all of them, the newest first, in pages. Deleted messages are never found. Letters other than a to z are matched with their case. Since API 1.17.

messages.fetchOlder.description: Asks the conversation's network for the history before the oldest message on this device, waits for it, and returns it as messages.list does, oldest first: the messages older than the oldest one the device had, with a cursor when more are stored. end is set when the network has no older history, or cannot give any. Since API 1.13.

messages.send.description: Sends a text message, since API 1.8 as an answer to another message (reply_to, when the conversation's actions allow it). The message is stored at once with status sending; its delivery is reported later by message.updated events. Since API 1.14, while the conversation's account is not connected, it is stored with status queued instead, and goes once the account connects, even after a restart.

messages.react.description: Adds the user's reaction to a message, then waits for the network's answer. The message changes at once (message.updated); when the network refuses, the reaction is taken back and the command fails with network. A reaction the user already made changes nothing. Since API 1.8.

messages.unreact.description: Takes back the user's reaction with this key, then waits for the network's answer, like messages.react. Without such a reaction, changes nothing. Since API 1.8.

messages.edit.description: Replaces the text of one of the user's text messages, then waits for the network's answer. The message changes at once (message.updated, edited); when the network refuses (for example a message too old to edit), the edit is undone and the command fails with network. Since API 1.8.

messages.delete.description: Deletes one of the user's messages for everyone, then waits for the network's answer. The message is erased from this device at once (message.updated, deleted), whatever the network answers: when it refuses, the command fails with network, and the message stays on the network. Since API 1.8. Since API 1.16, a queued message (still waiting for its account) is cancelled instead: erased on this device, never sent, whatever the network allows.

uploads.append.description: Adds a part of a media the user sends to an upload, and returns the upload's size so far. Without upload_id, starts a new upload. An upload holds at most 104857600 bytes (100 MiB); it lives in the core's memory until messages.sendMedia uses it, uploads.cancel drops it, it is left alone for 10 minutes, or the core stops. Since API 1.10.

uploads.cancel.description: Drops an upload. Dropping a used or unknown upload is not an error. Since API 1.10.

messages.sendMedia.description: Sends an upload as a photo, video, audio, voice or file message, with an optional caption, possibly as an answer to another message, when the conversation's actions take that kind. The upload is used up. As with messages.send, the message is stored at once with status sending; its delivery is reported later by message.updated events. Since API 1.10.

messages.forward.description: Sends a copy of a message to a conversation, on any network: its latest text, or its media (from this device's storage) with its caption, when that conversation's actions take that kind. The copy is a new message of the user's, sent like messages.send or messages.sendMedia; it answers nothing and does not say where it came from. Fails for a deleted message, and for media that is not on this device. Since API 1.26.

media.read.description: Reads a part of a message's media (or of its thumbnail), stored on this device. Media deleted with its message, or of a conversation no longer on this device, is not_found. Since API 1.9.

persons.list.description: Lists the persons the user merged conversations into, with their conversations on this device. A person whose conversations are all absent from this device (an account not added here) is not listed. Since API 1.2.

persons.create.description: Creates a person from one or more direct conversations, taken from the persons they belonged to. A person left without conversations is deleted (person.deleted). Since API 1.2.

persons.link.description: Links a direct conversation to a person, taking it from the person it belonged to. Since API 1.2.

persons.unlink.description: Unlinks a conversation from its person, if it has one. A person left without conversations is deleted. Since API 1.2.

persons.delete.description: Deletes a person. Their conversations stay, unlinked. Since API 1.2.

debug.ping.description: Returns its payload unchanged. Used to measure the cost of a call.

debug.stats.description: Returns the memory of the Go runtime after a garbage collection, for leak tests.

Events.description: Every event, by type, with the schema of its data.

account.updated.description: An account was added or its connection state changed.

account.verification.description: A step of an account's interactive verification (accounts.verification). Since API 1.22.

conversation.typing.description: Who is typing in a conversation changed: the names of those typing now (none: nobody). Not stored: after a restart nobody types. Since API 1.20.

conversation.deleted.description: A conversation was deleted, here (conversations.delete) or on its network. Its messages are gone with it. Since API 1.25.

conversation.updated.description: A conversation was created or changed: its name or kind, its person, its last message (sent after its message.added event, since API 1.4) or its read state (since API 1.4).

message.added.description: A message was stored: received, or sent from this device. Since API 1.7, edits, reactions and deletions are not messages: they come as message.updated events of the message they change.

message.updated.description: A stored message changed: its delivery status, or since API 1.7 its text (an edit), its reactions, or its deletion. The message is sent again in full. When it is its conversation's last message, a conversation.updated event follows.

person.updated.description: A person was created, renamed, or their conversations changed. The conversations whose person changed are sent again in conversation.updated events. Since API 1.2.

person.deleted.description: A person was deleted, lost their last conversation, or has none left on this device. Since API 1.2.

resync.required.description: The user interface read events too slowly and some were dropped: it must read the state again (accounts, conversations, persons, messages).

core.closed.description: The core was closed. It is the last event.

message.description: For developers and logs; user interfaces show their own text for each code.

ErrorCode.description: invalid_request: not a valid request envelope. unknown_command: no such command. invalid_params: the params do not match the command. not_found: an ID refers to nothing. unsupported: this core cannot do it (for example a login step type it does not know). timeout: the request took too long. cancelled: login.cancel ended the request. closed: the core is closed. network: the network failed or refused. internal: a bug or a local failure.

core_version.description: Version of the core build, for display and bug reports.

Network.description: A messaging network the core can connect to (Telegram, Signal...).

description.description: What adding an account of this network brings, in a short sentence for people who know nothing of Matrix or bridges. Omitted when the core has none. Since API 1.6.

login_flows.description: Ways to add an account, in order of preference.

name.description: The way to log in, worded to follow "Network:" ("With your phone number").

description.description: What the flow asks of the user, in a short sentence.

advanced.description: A flow that most people do not need (for developers, for example): user interfaces may show it apart from the others. Omitted when false. Since API 1.6.

Account.description: An account of the user on one network.

account_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it.

name.description: How the network names the account (phone number, username...). May be empty.

error.description: Explanation of the state for the user, when the network gave one.

connection.description: Where the account's bridge runs. Omitted by cores before API 1.12. Since API 1.12.

verification.description: For accounts whose devices are verified (Matrix): whether this device is, as other clients see it (accounts.verify). Omitted for other networks, and while the core does not know yet. Since API 1.15.

DeviceVerification.description: verified: signed by the account's cross-signing keys; other clients trust this device. unverified: not yet. Since API 1.15.

AccountConnection.description: on_device: the core on this device talks to the network itself; no server of Musubee sees the messages. hosted_bridge: a bridge on a server (Musubee's or the user's) talks to the network, and can read the messages it passes on. Since API 1.12.

AccountState.description: connecting: starting or catching up. connected: working. transient_disconnect: temporarily unreachable, the core retries. bad_credentials: the user must log in again. logged_out: the account was logged out. unknown_error: failed for another reason.

emoji.description: For emoji: the seven emoji to compare, in order.

reason.description: For cancelled: why, when the other device said.

VerificationStep.description: incoming: another device of the account asks to verify this one (accept or cancel). waiting: waiting for the other device. emoji: compare the emoji with the other device's (confirm or cancel). confirmed: confirmed here, waiting for the other device. done: this device is verified. cancelled: ended without verifying.

name.description: Its English name, as Matrix clients show it.

recovery_key.description: As the user typed or pasted it; spaces do not matter.

backup_restored.description: A key backup was found and its keys imported; false when the account has secure backup but no key backup.

account_id.description: The account to log in to again, from accounts.list. Since API 1.5.

values.description: The value of every field of the step, by field ID.

LoginStep.description: One step of a login process. user_input: show the fields and call login.submit. display_and_wait: show the display and call login.wait. complete: the account is added (account_id).

process_id.description: Identifies the login process in later login.* calls. Opaque.

step_id.description: Stable ID of this kind of step for the network (for example a 2FA password step), for user interfaces that customize some steps.

instructions.description: Text to show to the user, from the network. May be empty.

account_id.description: For complete steps: the account that was added.

field_id.description: Key of the value in login.submit.

pattern.description: A regular expression the value should match, for checking it before submitting.

options.description: For select fields: the allowed values.

LoginFieldType.description: A hint for the input control to show.

data.description: The text to encode as a QR code, the emoji or the code to show. Absent for nothing.

can_cancel.description: Whether the user interface may offer to go back (login.cancel).

conversation_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it.

person_id.description: The person this conversation is linked to, if any. Since API 1.2.

activity_ms.description: When the last message was sent, or when the conversation was created if it has none, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Conversation lists are ordered by it. A message.added event makes its message the last one. Since API 1.3.

last_message.description: The last message of the conversation, the one its thread shows last, if it has any. Since API 1.3.

unread_count.description: How many messages of others arrived after the user's read position: the last message the user read here or on another device, or their own last message, whichever is later. At most 1000; omitted when 0. Since API 1.4.

marked_unread.description: The user marked the conversation as unread (on another device, for now); reading it clears the flag. Omitted when false. Since API 1.4.

avatar_id.description: The conversation's picture, to read with media.read: a group's own, a direct conversation's contact's. Omitted when it has none. Since API 1.32.

archived.description: The user archived the conversation (conversations.archive). Omitted when false. Since API 1.31.

draft.description: The text the user left unsent in the conversation's composer (conversations.setDraft). Omitted when none. Since API 1.30.

pinned.description: The user pinned the conversation at the top of the inbox. Omitted when false. Since API 1.24.

muted_until_ms.description: The user muted the conversation, here or in another app of its network: when the mute ends, in Unix milliseconds, or -1 until unmuted. Omitted when not muted, or when the mute ended. Since API 1.23.

actions.description: What the conversation's network lets the user do to messages. Omitted when it allows none of them. Since API 1.8.

privacy.description: Who can read the conversation's messages besides its members. Omitted by cores before API 1.12. Since API 1.12.

seen.description: The user's latest message that others read, as their networks report, and who. Omitted when nobody read any, or the network does not report it. Since API 1.21.

message_id.description: The user's message that they read, or a later one.

names.description: The display names of those who read it, sorted by their IDs; "" for someone unnamed.

ConversationPrivacy.description: Who can read a conversation's messages besides the devices of its members, as far as the core knows. Since API 1.12.

readers.description: For network_can_read and bridge_can_read: who else can read, in the user's words, to put in a sentence ("Telegram", "the Matrix servers of the room's members"). Omitted otherwise.

PrivacyLevel.description: end_to_end: encrypted between the members' devices; no server can read. network_can_read: the network's servers can read (not end-to-end encrypted). bridge_can_read: encrypted up to a hosted bridge, which can read. device_only: a test network; the messages never leave this device. unknown: the core cannot tell; user interfaces must not claim more.

ConversationActions.description: Each action is omitted when the network does not allow it. The network may still refuse one message (for example one too old to edit): the command then fails.

media.description: messages.sendMedia, for the kinds of media listed. Omitted when the network takes none. Since API 1.10.

delete_chat.description: conversations.delete: direct conversations only, as networks delete groups for everyone. Since API 1.25.

MediaActions.description: The kinds of media a conversation takes; a kind is omitted when the network does not take it. Since API 1.10.

MediaAction.description: What a network takes of one kind of media. It may still refuse a media type: messages.sendMedia's message then fails. Since API 1.10.

max_size.description: The largest media it takes, in bytes. Omitted: the core's own limit (uploads.append).

caption.description: It takes a caption with this kind of media. Omitted when false.

mime_types.description: The media types it takes, as type/subtype, type/* or */*, without parameters. Omitted: any. Since API 1.11.

names.description: The display names of those typing, sorted; a name the core does not know is "" (someone types).

until_ms.description: When the mute ends, in Unix milliseconds; -1: until unmuted; 0: unmutes the conversation.

name.description: The member's name on the network; empty when the network gave none.

message_id.description: The last message the user read. Omitted: the conversation's last message.

account_id.description: Only the conversations of this account. A page may then hold fewer conversations than the limit, even none, with a cursor to the next.

before.description: A cursor from a previous result: return the conversations less recently active than the last one it returned. Since API 1.3.

limit.description: At most this many conversations (at most 200). Absent: all of them. Since API 1.3.

before.description: Present when more conversations may follow: the cursor to read them. Since API 1.3.

sender_avatar_id.description: The sender's picture, to read with media.read; for messages of others only. Omitted when they have none. Since API 1.33.

mentions_me.description: The message mentions the user (by name, or everyone in the room), as its network marked it, in its latest version. Omitted when false. Since API 1.28.

message_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it.

from_me.description: Sent by the user, from this device or another one.

sender_name.description: Display name of the sender. May be empty.

timestamp_ms.description: When the message was sent, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

text.description: The text of the message; for media kinds, the caption, often empty; for unsupported kinds, a fallback description.

error.description: For failed messages: why, for the user, when the network said.

edited.description: The sender changed the message after sending it: kind and text are those of its latest version. Omitted when false. Since API 1.7.

deleted.description: The message was deleted, by its sender or by the network: its kind is text and its text is empty, and it has no reactions nor reply_to. Omitted when false. Since API 1.7.

reactions.description: The reactions to the message, one per key, in the order of each key's first reaction. Omitted when there are none. Since API 1.7.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers, if it answers one. Since API 1.7.

media.description: The media of an image, video, audio, voice or file message. Omitted for other kinds, and for a deleted message. Since API 1.9.

MessageReaction.description: People who reacted to a message with the same key. Since API 1.7.

key.description: What they reacted with: usually an emoji, sometimes a short text.

count.description: How many people reacted with it, each counted once.

from_me.description: The user is one of them. Omitted when false.

names.description: The display names of the others who reacted, in the order they reacted, at most 10 (count says how many in all); a name the core does not know is left out. Omitted when there are none. Since API 1.19.

MessageReply.description: The message that another one answers, to quote it above the answer. Since API 1.7.

message_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it. The message may not be on this device (older than its history): then only message_id is given.

from_me.description: Sent by the user. Omitted when false.

sender_name.description: Display name of its sender. Omitted when empty.

text.description: Its text, as edited; for unsupported kinds, a fallback description. Omitted when empty.

deleted.description: It was deleted. Omitted when false.

kind.description: Its kind, when it is not text: an answered photo may have no text to quote. Omitted for text. Since API 1.9.

MessageMedia.description: The media of a message. Its bytes are read with media.read. Since API 1.9.

media_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it.

mime_type.description: The media type the network gave, such as image/jpeg; may be empty. It comes from the sender: user interfaces must never render active content (HTML, SVG, scripts) because of it.

file_name.description: The file's name. Omitted when unknown.

size.description: The size in bytes, when the network gave it.

width.description: In pixels, for images and videos, when known.

height.description: In pixels, for images and videos, when known.

duration_ms.description: For videos, audio and voice messages, when known.

animated.description: An animation (a GIF, or the short silent video that networks send for one): played on a loop, without sound nor controls. Omitted when false.

thumbnail_id.description: A smaller image to show until the media is read, to read with media.read. Omitted when there is none.

MessageKind.description: text: a normal message. notice: an automated message. emote: an action ("/me waves"). image, video, audio, voice (a recorded voice message) and file: a message with media, described by its media field, whose text is the caption (since API 1.9). unsupported: a kind this version cannot show; text holds a fallback.

MessageStatus.description: received: from someone else. sending, sent and failed: the delivery of a message from the user. queued: a message from the user that waits on this device for its account to connect, and goes then (since API 1.14).

before.description: A cursor from a previous result: return the messages before it. Absent: the latest messages.

limit.description: At most this many messages (default 50, at most 200).

query.description: The text to find, as typed; at most 200 characters.

conversation_id.description: The conversation to search. Omitted: every conversation.

before.description: A cursor from a previous result: the next page.

limit.description: At most this many messages (default 50, at most 200).

before.description: Cursor for the next page; absent when there is none.

limit.description: At most this many messages in the result (default 50, at most 200); the network may give more, which stay on the device for messages.list.

messages.description: Oldest first; empty when the network gave nothing.

before.description: Cursor for older messages already on the device (messages.list); absent when there are none.

end.description: The network has no older history, or cannot give history: asking again changes nothing. Omitted when false.

before.description: Cursor for the older messages; absent when there are none.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers, in the same conversation. Since API 1.8.

upload_id.description: The upload to add to, from a previous result. Omitted: a new upload.

data.description: The next bytes, in base64 (RFC 4648, with padding): at most 1048576 bytes (1 MiB) once decoded.

upload_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it.

size.description: The bytes the upload holds so far.

message_id.description: The message to copy, in any conversation.

upload_id.description: An upload of uploads.append, with at least one byte.

kind.description: How the media is sent: image, video, audio, voice or file.

mime_type.description: The media type, such as image/jpeg. Empty when unknown.

caption.description: A text sent with the media, when the conversation's actions take one for this kind.

width.description: In pixels, for images and videos, when known.

height.description: In pixels, for images and videos, when known.

duration_ms.description: For videos, audio and voice messages, when known.

reply_to.description: The message this one answers, in the same conversation.

media_id.description: A media_id or thumbnail_id of a message.

length.description: How many bytes to read at most (default and maximum 1048576, 1 MiB): larger media is read in several calls.

size.description: The size of the whole media, in bytes.

data.description: The bytes read, in base64 (RFC 4648, with padding): fewer than asked at the end of the media, none from its end on.

Person.description: A person of the user's, and the conversations with them that the user merged. Since API 1.2.

person_id.description: Opaque: user interfaces must not parse it.

conversation_ids.description: The person's conversations on this device, in the order they were linked.

name.description: Not blank, at most 256 bytes in UTF-8. The name of the first conversation if absent.
Not blank, at most 256 bytes in UTF-8.
